<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|90|THE GOSPEL|CHA. II.}}</noinclude>Holy Ghost appeareth in the likenesse of a doue, the Sonne also is recommended vnto vs. ''Ambros. li. 1 de Sacram. c. 5''.

''12. Desert.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Christs example of penance.}}Christ doing penance by long fasting, solitarinesse, and conuersing with wilde beastes, gaue example and instruction to the Church for Lent fast, and to holy Eremites of retiring them selues to the wildernesse and prayer.

''35. Desert place.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Solitarie contemplation.}}Christ vsed very often to retire into solitary places, no doubt for our example, to teach vs that such places are best for prayer and contemplation, and that we should often retire our selues from worldly matters to solitary meditation of heauenly things.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. II.}}}}}}

{{c|''Against the Scribes and Pharisees he defendeth first his povver to remitte sinnes in earth, 23 and his eating vvith sinners (as being the Physicion of soules, signified in those his miraculous cures vpon bodies): 18 then also he defendeth his Disciples, not hauing as yet any fastes by him prescribed vnto them, and plucking eares of corne vpon the Sabboth: signifying vvithal that he vvil change their ceremonies.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}}}ND againe he entred into Capharnaum after some daies, and it vvas heard that he vvas in the house,{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 9, 1. Lu. 5, 18.''}} {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}}† and many came together, so that there vvas no place no not at the doore, and he spake to them the vvord. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}}† And they came to him bringing one sicke of the palsey, vvho vvas caried of foure. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}}† And vvhen they could not offer him vnto him for the multitude, they {{sup|‖}} vncouered the roofe vvhere he vvas: and opening it they did let dovvne the couche vvherein the sicke of the palsey lay. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=5}}† And vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} had seen {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Lord is moued to be merciful to sinners by other mens faith and desires, and not only by the parties owne meanes alvvay.}}∷ their faith, he saith to the {{sup|‖}} sicke of the palsey, Sonne, {{sup|‖}} thy sinnes are forgiuen thee. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=6}}† And there vvere certaine of the Scribes sitting there and thinking in their hartes, {{verse|chapter=2|verse=7}}† Why doth he speake so? he blasphemeth. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Iob. 14, 4. Esa. 43, 25.''}}* Who can forgiue sinnes but only God? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=8}}† Which by and by {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving in his spirit, that they so thought vvithin them selues, saith to them, Why thinke you these things in your hartes? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=9}}† Whether is easier, to say to the sicke of the palsey, Thy sinnes are forgiuen thee: or to say, Arise, take vp thy couche, and vvalke? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=10}}† But that you may knovv that {{sup|‖}} the Sonne of man hath povver {{sup|‖}} in earth to forgiue sinnes (he saith to the sicke of the palsey) {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11}}† I say to thee, Arise, take vp thy couche, and goe into thy house. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=12}}† And forthvvith he arose: and taking vp his couche, vvent his vvay in the sight of al, so that al marueled, and glorified God, saying, That vve neuer savv the like.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=13}}† And he vvent forth againe to the sea: and al the multitude came to him, and he taught them. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14}}† And vvhen he<noinclude>{{rh|||passed}}</noinclude>
